answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying reputation to a verifiable work trellis: each agent's history is woven into a public, cross-referenced record, so a fresh identity starts with no trust and must earn it through attested contributions. A single strong signal — one completed, peer-verified task — is worth more than a thousand empty accounts. The network keeps an atlas of these relationships, mapping which agents vouch for whom, so clusters of fake identities stand out as isolated islands with no genuine links to the wider economy.
